Name: Notifying local elected officials of certain stop work orders.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to notifying local elected officials of certain stop work orders

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Housing and Buildings

Summary: This bill would require that the Department of Buildings (DOB) (1) provide immediate notice to council members and borough presidents of class 1 and class 2 stop work orders issued in their geographic electoral region, and (2) every two weeks, provide council members and borough presidents with a summary of class 1 and class 2 stop work orders that were issued and rescinded in the previous two weeks, as well as any class 1 or class 2 violations that remain uncorrected.

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:\ulnone\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\qj\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi720\sl480\slmult1\qj\tx1080 Section 1. Article 207 of chapter 2 of title 28 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding new sections 28-207.2.1.1 and 28-207.2.1.2 to read as follows:\par
\pard\ltrpar\sl276\slmult1\qj\tx1080\ul\b\'a7 28-207-2.1.1 Immediate notice to elected officials.\b0  Within 24 hours of issuing a stop work order in response to a class 1 or class 2 violation, as defined in subdivision (b) of section 102-01 of title 1 of the rules of the city of New York, the commissioner shall notify the council member of the district and the president of the borough in which the building work that is the subject of such stop work order is being executed. Such notice shall include the address of the building work, the issuance date of the stop work order, the classification of the violation, and the reason for the issuance.\par
\par
\b\'a7 28-207.2.1.2 Summary report to elected officials.\b0  Beginning on April 1, 2027, and every two weeks thereafter, the commissioner shall provide a report that meets the specifications of this section to each council member and borough president on stop work orders affecting the district or borough they represent. Such report shall include the following information about each such stop work order that was issued or rescinded in the previous two weeks in connection with a class 1 or class 2 violation, as defined in subdivision (b) of section 102-01 of title 1 of the rules of the city of New York, as well as all class 1 or class 2 violations that remain uncorrected:\par
\par
\pard\ltrpar\fi-360\li720\sa240\sl276\slmult1\qj 1. \tab Address of the building work affected by the stop work order;\par
2. \tab Issuance date of the stop work order;\par
3. \tab Classification of the violation, as defined in subdivision (b) of section 102-01 of title 1 of the rules of the city of New York;\par
4. \tab Reason for the issuance of the stop work order;\par
5. \tab Penalties imposed by the department in connection with the stop work order;\par
6. \tab Rescission date of the stop work order, where applicable; and\par
7. \tab Reason for the rescission of the stop work order, where applicable.\par
\pard\ltrpar\qj\ulnone\'a7 2. This local law takes effect immediately.\fs18\par
